blocks.text: Rowan Bell checking in with Nell about tool library upkeep and recent activity.

We had a garden fork come back last week with two tines bent right over. Someone must've hit a root. I got it in the bench vise, worked it straight with the mallet, then filed down the burrs so it wouldn't snag. It's back on the shelf now.

Then Saturday was the mower clinic. Six people showed up. We went through the whole process: safe removal of the blade, sharpening with a file—I stressed keeping the original bevel—and how to check the balance by hanging it on a nail. A couple of folks brought their own mowers and did the work right there. They seemed pleased to know they could do it themselves next time.
Thinking about one for pruning tool maintenance before the spring rush. Saw sharpening, pivot bolt tightening, that sort of thing. I'll put a note on the board next month to see if there's interest.
